memoryText: I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read John 14:6 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Jesus says this to Thomas in the upper room, on the last night before the cross. Thomas had asked, “How can we know the way?” and Jesus’ answer is not a set of directions but himself.

“I am the way.” Jesus is not just a guide who points. He is the road itself. We come to God not by our efforts, rituals, or goodness, but by Jesus. His death opens the path to God.

“And the truth.” He is the reality behind all the shadows of the Old Testament, and the truth about God. Everything he says is true because he is truth.

“And the life.” He gives life that death cannot end. He is the source of it, the one who raised Lazarus and who rose himself.

“No one comes to the Father except through me.” This is exclusive and it is gracious. It is exclusive because there is only one way. It is gracious because the way is open to anyone who comes. No one is turned away.

When you wonder if you are on the right path, or when someone asks how a person can know God, say this verse. The way is a person, and he is here.
weekInReview: This week Jesus declared that his sheep will never perish and that no one can snatch them from his hand. You stood at Lazarus’s tomb and heard him say, “I am the resurrection and the life.” You saw Mary pour out costly perfume and Jesus speak of the grain of wheat that must fall into the earth and die. In the Upper Room, he washed his disciples’ feet, gave a new commandment, and comforted them with the promise of the Father’s house, the Way, and the Helper. The Psalms were a chorus of the shepherd: Psalm 23, the LORD is my shepherd; Psalm 100, we are the sheep of his pasture; and Psalm 103, bless the LORD, O my soul, who forgives all your iniquity.
reflectionQuestions: Jesus said no one can snatch his sheep out of his hand. How does this security affect how you think about doubt and failure?
At the Last Supper, Jesus washed feet and gave a new commandment to love one another. Who is one person you could serve or love this week in a way that costs you something?
Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life. What does it mean to you that the way to the Father is a person and not a program?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus that he is the way, truth, and life.
Thank him that his sheep are safe in his hand.
